title: Cloud Computing
subtitle: A Lumenary CS elective: how computing became a utility, and how to build on it well — virtualisation and containers, networking and storage, Kubernetes, serverless, infrastructure as code, observability, security, cost, and the AI cloud of 2026.
description: This elective of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) teaches cloud computing from the inside: what actually happens when you rent a virtual machine, run a container or deploy a function, and how professionals build systems that are reliable, secure and affordable on someone else's computers. It turns Lumenary CS's [distributed systems](/en/cs/distributed-systems/), [system design](/en/cs/system-design/) and [reliability engineering](/en/cs/reliability-engineering/) into practice on real platforms.

It assumes Lumenary CS up to its Scale level. Python blocks with a **Run in browser** button run in the browser and simulate what is too big to run there — a scheduler, a load balancer, an autoscaler, a cost model; configuration for Kubernetes, Terraform and the cloud providers is shown and explained, not run. The major providers (Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud and others) and open-source projects are described side by side.

It is written to inform, not to sell: tools and companies are named fairly and by link, and the lessons are as plain about costs, failures and trade-offs as about what works. Every lesson was drafted with AI assistance and is awaiting review by a human expert. The text, exercises and code are original and licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 (code Apache-2.0). Papers, specifications and projects' own documentation are linked, not retold.
